title: Irreducibility of the generic fibre of a dominant map
statement: Let f:X -> S be a dominant morphism of schemes with X irreducible, and eta a generic point of S. Then the scheme-theoretic fibre X_eta is irreducible. No reducedness, flatness or finite-type assumption is required. Dominance, irreducibility and scheme fibres use [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] and [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Conventions: irreducibility of the underlying topological space [def-weil-irreducible-components].

proof.text: The continuous image of the source generic point is generic for the closure of the image. Dominance identifies that closure with S, so uniqueness of generic points puts the source generic point over eta. In the topological fibre every pair of nonempty relative opens contains this point. Hence the topological fibre is irreducible. Transport along Scheme.Hom.fiberHomeo to the scheme fibre.
